entries.title: The admin panel (operators)
q: how do i open the admin panel
server admin tools for the mod
entries.answer: Operators have an admin panel with every admin action on one screen. Bind its key in Options, Controls (it starts unbound).
more: Operators have an admin panel: a search box over every action, areas (Town, Ages, People, Army & War, Economy, Build, Events, World, Debug) and recent actions down the left; the town it acts on and a live status strip across the top; the area's actions in the middle with their values, Dry run and Run; the town's inspect report and running jobs on the right.
steps: Press it, pick a town and an area, choose an action, set its values.
Dry run to see what it would do, then Run. A destructive action asks to confirm and offers a snapshot first.
controls: Admin panel key (set it in Options → Controls)
tips: The panel runs each action on the server with your permissions, exactly as the matching command would.
warn: Operators only. The server's admin config can switch the tools off or raise the permission level they need.

entries.title: Server settings: the common config
q: how do i turn off raids
entries.answer: Server owners set the towns in config/mc_assistant-common.toml, under [villages]: raids, wars, growth, natural towns, build speed and more.
more: Server owners set the towns in config/mc_assistant-common.toml, section [villages]: naturalVillages, villageRaids, villageWars, villageBreeding and villageGrowthCap, villageWorldCap, villageBuildSpeed (percent), villageReshapeLand (off keeps terrain), villageColonies, villagesShareGoods, villagePhantoms, villageDisasters, replaceVillagers (the old takeover, off), townBorders, battleView and more.
tips: Founding rules live there too: foundingWho, foundingTownsPerPlayer, foundingFreeKit, foundingNeedsItem, foundingTravel, foundingSiteReach, foundingHints, villageFoundingMost, villageCharterFolk.
warn: Restart the server (or reload configs) after editing.

entries.title: Founding rules (who may found towns)
entries.answer: Who may found towns, and how many, is set in config/mc_assistant-common.toml: foundingWho and foundingTownsPerPlayer.
more: foundingWho (everyone, citizens or operators; operators always may), foundingTownsPerPlayer (3; 0 for no limit), foundingFreeKit (a kit on first join), foundingNeedsItem (founding uses a kit, spawner or charter), foundingTravel and foundingTravelReach (Take me there), foundingSiteReach (160), foundingHints, villageFoundingMost (500) and villageCharterFolk (70).

entries.title: Keeping a server light: folk limits and performance
q: how to reduce lag from towns
entries.answer: Every folk costs the server a little, so keep towns modest and use the growth and world caps in the common config.
more: Every folk is a ticking creature: hundreds are heavy.

Keep towns modest at founding, and use villageGrowthCap (largest a town grows by children, 100), villageWorldCap (the world's folk, 200), villageFoundingMost, the town level-of-detail settings (townLod...) that let far towns sleep, and the tick budgets (townTickBudgetMs, pathBudgetMs).
tips: Clients can turn down how much of the folk's life is drawn in the client animation config.

entries.title: The admin toolkit's switches
entries.answer: The server config's admin section switches the admin tools on or off and sets who may use them.
more: The server config's admin section switches the admin toolkit: adminTools on or off, the permission level it needs, the level for destructive actions, how long a confirm stands, and the entity-count warning.

entries.title: Your own client settings
entries.answer: Your own settings (toasts, the tracker, the inventory coin, name tags, ambience) are in the config folder's mc_assistant client files.
more: Your own settings, on your computer: config/mc_assistant-ui-client.toml (favourites' toasts and tracker, the weekly summary and bill toasts, the inventory coin button) and config/mc_assistant-client.toml (name tags and their range, ambience sounds, effects, marks, faces, the emote camera).
tips: Name tags and the lens are quicker to set in the camera screen (K).
